paras.text: Robert Schumann once said, “The laws of morals are those of art.” What the great man is saying here is that there is good music and bad music. The greatest music, even if it’s tragic in nature, ① taking us to a world higher than ours; somehow the beauty uplifts us. Bad music, on the other hand, degrades us. It’s the same with performances: a bad performance isn’t ② necessarily the result of incompetence. Some of the worst performances occur when the performers, ③ no matter how accomplished, are thinking more of themselves than of the music they’re playing. These doubtful characters aren’t really listening to what the composer is saying — they’re just showing off, ④ hoping that they’ll have a great ‘success’ with the public. The performer’s basic task is to try to understand the meaning of the music, and then ⑤ to communicate it honestly to others.

paras.text: Most people have a perfect time of day ①when they feel they are at their best, whether in the morning, evening, or afternoon. Some of us are night owls, some early birds, and others in between may feel most ②actively during the afternoon hours. If you are able to organize your day and divide your work,make ③that a point to deal with tasks that demand attention at your best time of the day. However, if the task you face demands creativity and novel ideas, it’s best to tackle it at your “worst” time of day! So if you are an early bird, make sure ④to attack your creative task in the evening, and vice versa for night owls. When your mind and body are less alert than at your“peak” hours, the muse of creativity ⑤awakens and is allowed to roam more freely. In other words, when your mental machinery is loose rather than standing at attention, the creativity flows.
